newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan party decides to end special income tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Japan party decides to end special income tax cut.

text.p: A tax system panel of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) on Wednesday finalised a plan to revise the nation's tax system in the next fiscal year from April 1, including an end to special income tax cuts, panel chairman Yoshiro Hayashi told a news conference.
The party proposal is expected to be approved as a government plan later this month, government officials said.
A government advisory panel is due to adopt its own tax reform plan later on Wednesday, but the contents will be almost exactly in line with the party plan.
The party tax reform plan confirmed a government decision that Japan's consumption tax will be raised to five percent from three percent on April 1.
The party, however, decided not to carry out major changes to the corporate tax system or to the tax system on land holdings in 1997/98.
"We may have left an impression that we are putting off decisions on the key issues, but we will consider necessary revisions when concrete moves toward changes in those taxes emerge," Hayashi said.

The panel also decided to raise taxes on domestic liquor known as "shochu" by up to 2.4 times, and to cut whiskey taxes by around 58 percent over a two-year period in order to comply with a World Trade Organisation (WTO) ruling, Hayashi said.
The WTO, ruling on a complaint by the European Union, the United States and Canada, said in November that Japan taxes foreign spirits at levels higher than those for domestic liquor.
A senior LDP official said the European Union has accepted the tax revision. He said the United States may also accept the plan.
